chose: 4.4 B for session-start is a FACTS-level cache, not an output cache. Cache a trimmed "digest state" per record in .sofar/.index/digest/<slug>.json. It holds the finalized InitiativeState with every unbounded collection cut to exactly the members renderStatus and its helpers can reach: sessions (last with summary, last unwritten with activity, the unwritten list, open sessions, overlapping write-backs), with files_touched dropped. The key is the log's size + mtimeMs + engine + schema, and a miss folds and rewrites. Every live input (session id, git, repo memory, neighbours, rules, notices, env switches) stays live and is passed to renderStatus unchanged. The cut rule is enforced by a parity suite, not by argument: renderStatus(digestState(s), o) must equal renderStatus(s, o) byte for byte over every real log in this repo, the team100 corpus and the status fixtures, across a matrix of options. It runs in both implementations, TS first then the Rust mirror. The file-states index read (refresh_file_states, ~25% of session-start at team100) is the next cost after that. It belongs to record-index's index format, so it is named here and not changed.
over: An output cache keyed by every input: it can never hit, because the output carries `Session: <id>`, session-start fires once per session, and the notices carry clock-derived ages. Also over caching the full edge-free state: 14 MB at team100 is ~140 ms to parse in the core.
because: Session-start profile at team100 (2026-09-23, under load, relative): fold 316 of 523 samples, refresh_file_states 128 (index JSON parse 80), render_status 40 (open_session_file_conflicts 33), attribution 11. The options (repo memory, neighbours, rules, notices) take part in renderStatus's cap arithmetic, so the state part cannot be rendered once and composed. The only exact route that skips the fold is a smaller state that provably renders the same, and "provably" here means a byte-parity suite over real and synthetic records.
